<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par95 />From a stem {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}} ({{GHGheb|text=דָּלָה}}, cf., however, Barth, {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZDMG.|Zeitschrift der deutschen morgenländischen Gesellschaft, Lpz. 1846 ff., since 1903 ed. by A. Fischer.}}}} 1887, p. 607, who assumes a stem {{GHGheb|text=ידל}}) the masculine {{GHGheb|text=דַּל}} appears to have been formed after the rejection of the final {{GHGterm|Yôdh}}, and afterwards the feminine {{GHGheb|text=דֶּ֫לֶת|translate=door}}; but in the ''plural'' {{GHGheb|text=דְּלָתוֹת}}, {{GHGterm|constr.}} {{GHGheb|text=דַּלְתוֹת}}, the {{GHGheb|text=ת}} of the termination is retained (see above, d, {{GHGheb|text=חֲנִיתוֹת}}). In a similar way {{GHGheb|text=רְפָתִים|translate=stalls}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hb|chapter=3|verse=17}}, has arisen, if it is from the stem {{GHGheb|text=רפה}}, and {{GHGheb|text=שֹׁקֶת|translate=trough}} (from {{GHGheb|text=שָׁקָה}}), of which the masc. must have been {{GHGheb|text=שֹׁק}} = {{GHGheb|text=שֳׁקִי}}; on the other hand, the ''plur. constr.'' {{GHGheb|text=שִֽׁקֲתוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=30|verse=38}} (again retaining the feminine {{GHGheb|text=ת}} as an apparent radical) can only be an abnormal formation from the ''singular'' {{GHGheb|text=שֹׁ֫קֶת}}, not from a kindred form {{GHGheb|text=שֶׁ֫קֶת}} or {{GHGheb|text=שֵׁ֫קֶת}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|95|g}}
2. Paradigm II: ground-form ''qăṭălăt'', &c., cf. {{GHGpar|94|c}}, Paradigm II, ''a'' and ''b''. Analogous to the masculine forms like {{GHGheb|text=קָטָן}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=קְטַנִּים}}, we find {{GHGheb|text=קְטַנָּה|translate=parva}}, &c.—The {{GHGterm|constr.}} forms, like {{GHGheb|text=צִדְקַת}} (''ṣidh<sup>e</sup>qăth''), are distinguished by the vocal {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}} ({{GHGpar|10|d}}) from the segholate forms, like {{GHGheb|text=כִּבְשַּׂת}} (''kibh-săth''). Consequently the ''constr. st.'' {{GHGheb|text=בִּרְכַּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=28|verse=4}}, &c. (from {{GHGheb|text=בְּרָכָה|translate=blessing}}), and {{GHGheb|text=חֶרְדַּת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=14|verse=15}}, &c. (from {{GHGheb|text=חֲרָדָה|translate=a trembling}}), are abnormal.—Under the influence of a guttural (see Paradigm ''b'') the original ''ă'' is retained in the first syllable in the ''constr. st.'' (cf. also {{GHGheb|text=אֲדָמָה|translate=earth}}, {{GHGheb|text=אַדְמַת}}); in other cases it is modified to {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=עֲגָלָה|translate=wagon}}, {{GHGheb|text=עֶגְלָתוֹ}}. Frequently from an ''absol. st.'' in {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}} the {{GHGterm|constr.}} is formed with the termination {{GHGheb|text=ת}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=עֲטָרָה|translate=crown}}, constr. {{GHGheb|text=עֲטֶ֫רֶת}} (from {{GHGheb|text=עֲטַרְתְּ}}); along with {{GHGheb|text=עֲצָרָה|translate=assembly}}, {{GHGheb|text=עֲצֶ֫רֶת}} is found usually, even in the ''absol. st.''; {{GHGheb|text=יְבֶ֫מֶת}} (from {{GHGheb|text=יָבָם|translate=levir}}) before suffixes is pointed as in {{GHGheb|text=יְבִמְתִּי}}, and thus entirely agrees with {{GHGheb|text=גְּבֶ֫רֶת}} (Paradigm I ''e''). From a stem {{GHGheb|text=(אָמַן) ל״ן}} is formed {{GHGheb|text=אֱמֶת|translate=truth}} (from ''ʾaɨmant'', and this no doubt for an original ''ʾămint'', {{GHGpar|69|c}}) before suffixes {{GHGheb|text=אֲמִתִּי}}, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|95|h}}
From the masc. form {{GHGheb|text=קָטֵל}} (''qăṭĭl'') are formed, according to rule, {{GHGheb|text=גְּדֵרָה|translate=wall}}, {{GHGheb|text=נְבֵלָה|translate=corpse}}, constr. {{GHGheb|text=נִבְלַת}}; {{GHGheb|text=בְּהֵמָה|translate=cattle}}, constr. {{GHGheb|text=בֶּֽהֱמַת}} (for {{GHGheb|text=בַּֽהֲמַת}}), with suffix {{GHGheb|text=בְּהֶמְתְּךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=19|verse=19}}. More frequently, however, the ''ē'' of the second syllable is retained before the termination ''ath'' of the ''constr. st.''; thus from {{GHGheb|text=נְבֵלָה}} once {{GHGheb|text=נְבֵֽלָתִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=26|verse=19}}, and always {{GHGheb|text=בְּרֵכַת|translate=pool}}, {{GHGheb|text=גְּזֵלַת|translate=prey}}, {{GHGheb|text=טְמֵאַת|translate=unclean}}, {{GHGheb|text=מְלֵֽאֲתִי|translate=full}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=21}} (with ''Ḥireq compaginis'', see {{GHGpar|90|l}}), {{GHGheb|text=מְרֵֽרָתִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=16|verse=13}}; {{GHGheb|text=שְׁאֵֽלָתִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=1|verse=27}}, &c. (with elision of the {{GHGheb|text=א}}, {{GHGheb|text=שֵֽׁלָתֵךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=1|verse=17}}), also {{GHGheb|text=שֶֽׁאֱלָתִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=6|verse=8}}. Cf. the analogous forms of the ''constr. st.'' {{GHGheb|text=מַגֵּפַת|translate=plague}}, {{GHGheb|text=תַּרְדֵּמַת|translate=deep sleep}}, from {{GHGheb|text=מַגֵּפָה}}, {{GHGheb|text=תַּרְדֵּמָה}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|95|i}}
As dual we find {{GHGheb|text=יַרְכָתַ֫יִם|translate=sides}} (cf. {{GHGheb|text=יַרְכָתוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=49|verse=13}}, from the obsolete {{GHGheb|text=יְרֵכָה}}, feminine of {{GHGheb|text=יָרֵךְ}}); the ''constr. st.'' {{GHGheb|text=יַרְכְּתֵי}} is perhaps to be referred to a segholate form ({{GHGheb|text=יַרְכָּה}}, cf. {{GHGheb|text=יֶ֫רֶךְ}} as ''constr. st.'' of {{GHGheb|text=יָרֵךְ}}), unless the closed syllable be due to the analogy of {{GHGheb|text=בִּרְכַּת}} and {{GHGheb|text=חֶרְדַּת}} (see g).

{{GHGmargin-letter|95|k}}
In the forms with simple {{GHGheb|text=ת}} feminine the ground-form ''qăṭĭlt'' is developed ({{GHGpar|69|c}}) to ''q<sup>e</sup>ṭalt'', and this again regularly to {{GHGheb|text=קְטֶ֫לֶת}}. Thus the feminine of {{GHGheb|text=הָבֵר|translate=companion}} is {{GHGheb|text=חֲבֶ֫רֶת}} (with suffix {{GHGheb|text=חֲבֶרְתָּהּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mal|chapter=2|verse=14}}, cf. {{GHGheb|text=שְׁכֶנְתָּהּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=3|verse=22}}), of {{GHGheb|text=גָּדֵר}} fem. {{GHGheb|text=גְּדֶ֫רֶת}} besides {{GHGheb|text=גְּדֵרָה}}.—Of {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}} stems the segholate forms {{GHGheb|text=נַ֫חַת|translate=rest}} and {{GHGheb|text=שַׁ֫חַת|translate=pit}} (from {{GHGheb|text=נוּחַ}}, {{GHGheb|text=שׁוּחַ}}) belong to this class; Böttcher (''Gram.'' i. 411) rightly distinguished the latter from {{GHGheb|text=שַׁ֫חַת|translate=corruption}} (stem {{GHGheb|text=שָׁחַת}}); in the same way also {{GHGheb|text=נַ֫חַת|translate=rest}} is distinct from {{GHGheb|text=נַ֫חַת|translate=a lighting down}} (stem {{GHGheb|text=נָחַת}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|95|l}}
The feminines of the form ''qăṭĭl'' from stems {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}}, as {{GHGheb|text=מֵתָה|translate=mortua}}, {{GHGheb|text=עֵדָה}} fem.<section end=par95 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
